Tinea Pedis (Athlete’s Foot), Tinea Manuum and Tinea Cruris

Tinea Pedis is a common fungal infection of the toes, while Tinea Manuum affects the palms and interdigital spaces. Both Tinea Pedis and Manuum are often the source of infection at other sites, especially the groin (Tinea Cruris).

Mycetoma is a chronic disease usually of the foot, but any part of the body can be affected. Infection is most probably acquired by traumatic inoculation of fungi (eumycetoma) or bacteria (actinomycetoma) into the subcutaneous tissue.
